scene.intro: Click a part to pick it up, then click a highlighted place. Cyan places can take it; amber ones cannot, and clicking one tells you why. Everything here can also be done in the list below. The camera stays where you leave it while you select and install parts. Move it yourself with the view controls, drag, or zoom.

scene.benchAssembly: Prepare the motherboard on the workbench first: CPU, RAM, M.2 drive and CPU cooler/block. Then select the motherboard and place it in the case; its attached parts move with it. Finish with the graphics card, power supply, case fans, radiator and cables. A SATA drive mounts in the case.

help.part: The {part} goes in the glowing {place}. Tap it there.
help.ram: Bring the module over a free slot whose clip is open, notch facing the slot's key. For two modules the board's manual recommends {rec}.

explain.cpu: The CPU is the PC's brain. The lever presses it onto hundreds of contacts in the socket.
explain.ram: RAM is short-term memory. For two modules this board's manual recommends {rec}, so they run in dual channel.
explain.ramNoRec: RAM is short-term memory. This board's manual gives no slot recommendation; each module goes in its own slot.
explain.storage: The M.2 SSD keeps Windows and your files. One small screw holds it down.
explain.cooler: The cooler pulls heat away from the CPU. Its fan plugs into CPU_FAN later.
explain.motherboard: Small parts are easier to fit on the bench. Then the board moves into the case with them on it.
explain.gpu: The graphics card draws the picture. It goes in the top PCIe x16 slot.
explain.psu: The power supply turns wall power into the voltages the parts need.
explain.atx: The 24-pin lead powers the motherboard. It only fits one way.
explain.cpuPower: The CPU gets its own 8-pin power lead, at the top of the board.
explain.gpuPower: The graphics card needs its own 8-pin PCIe power.
explain.cpuFan: CPU_FAN lets the board control and watch the cooler's fan.
explain.powerSwitch: These tiny pins connect the case's power button to the board.
explain.caseFan: Case fans move air through the case to keep everything cool.
explain.power: Start runs the same checks as a real first boot: power, CPU, memory and storage.
explain.done: Every part and cable is in place, and the PC passed its startup checks.
explain.cpu2: The Core i9-14900K uses the same LGA1700 socket and looks almost the same as the i5. Here it is set to need the liquid cooler.
explain.aio: A liquid cooler pumps coolant from the block on the CPU through two hoses to a radiator, where two 140 mm fans blow the heat out of the case.
explain.aioPump: AIO_PUMP powers the pump that moves the coolant. Without it the liquid stands still.
explain.aioFan: The radiator fans plug into CPU_FAN, so the board speeds them up as the CPU warms.
explain.liquidRule: This is a lab rule for this one CPU: the Core i9 here starts only with the 280 mm liquid cooler. Real PCs depend on the cooler's rating and the CPU's power limits.
explain.fan: A case fan moves air through the case. The arrows on its frame show the airflow.
explain.sata: A SATA drive needs two cables: data to the board, power from the PSU.
explain.argb: ARGB is 5 V, 3 pins. It never goes on a 12 V RGB header. Lighting is optional.

companion.noAi: I can answer What next?, Help me and Explain this step. Open questions need the AI tutor set up on the server.

hands.cpuOpen: Plate open. Now turn the CPU so its triangle meets the socket's mark.
hands.cpuTurn: Turn the CPU until its triangle matches the socket's mark.
hands.cpuCentre: Centre it over the socket, then lower it gently.
hands.cpuLowered: It sits flat in the socket. Close the plate, then lock the lever.
hands.cpuLowerFirst: Lower the CPU fully before closing the plate.
hands.cpuClosed: Locked in. The cover popped off: keep it for later.
hands.coolerOver: The cooler is on top. Take the cooler off first.
hands.ramOpen: Latch open. Line the notch up with the slot's key.
hands.ramOpenBoth: This slot has a clip at each end: open both first.
hands.ramTurn: Turn the stick round: the notch must meet the slot's key.
hands.ramCentre: It's over the slot but not lined up. Move it until it sits right above the groove.
hands.ramIn: Click! It's home and the latch closed.
hands.ramReleased: Latch open: the stick lifted. Press it in again or lift it out.
hands.lifted: Out and back on the bench.
hands.cpuReleased: Plate open. You can lift the CPU out now.
hands.gpuCoversFirst: First take out the case's slot covers beside the top slot, so the card's bracket has somewhere to go.
hands.gpuLatchFirst: Push the slot's latch open before the card goes in.
hands.gpuOpen: Slot ready. Turn the card so its bracket faces the case's rear and line it up.
hands.gpuTurn: The card is turned the wrong way; its bracket must face the back of the case.
hands.gpuCentre: The card is off the slot; line the gold edge up with the slot and the bracket with the opening.
hands.gpuIn: Card seated and the latch clicked. Now screw its bracket to the case.
hands.gpuScrewed: Bracket screwed. The card is secure.
hands.gpuUnscrewed: Screws out. Press the latch to release the card.
hands.gpuReleased: Latch released. You can lift the card out now.
hands.gpuUnplug: Unplug the card's power cable first.
hands.gpuUnscrew: Take the bracket screws out first.
hands.gpuReleaseFirst: Press the slot's latch to release the card first.
hands.gpuSeatFirst: Push the card fully in before screwing the bracket.
hands.coversOut: Covers out. The card's bracket fits there now.
hands.coversBlocked: A card is in that opening; take it out before refitting the covers.
hands.closeBlocked: That latch can't move like that right now.
hands.m2Open: Latch open. Turn the drive so its notch matches the slot's ridge, and line it up.
hands.m2OpenFirst: Turn the M.2 Q-Latch to unlock before the drive goes in.
hands.m2Turn: The drive is the wrong way round; its notch must line up with the ridge in the slot.
hands.m2Centre: The drive is off the slot; slide it along until the connector sits right in front of the slot.
hands.m2Lowered: In at an angle. Now press it flat and turn the Q-Latch to lock it.
hands.m2Closed: Q-Latch locked. The drive is held flat.
hands.m2Released: Latch unlocked; the drive springs up. You can slide it out now.
hands.m2LowerFirst: Push the drive fully into the slot first.
hands.pasteOn: Paste on. A small amount is enough; the cooler's pressure spreads it.
hands.filmOff: Film off. Don't touch the plate now.
hands.standoffsOk: Standoffs checked: they match the board's holes.
hands.fanTurned: Fan turned. Check the arrow before you fix it.
hands.coolerPlaced: Resting on the CPU. Tighten the corners across the diagonal.
hands.screwDiagonal: Next, the opposite corner: {corner}. Across the diagonal keeps the pressure even.
hands.liquidPrep: Paste first: put a small drop on the CPU before the pump block goes on.
hands.pickPort: First pick which socket this end goes into.

reversed.latch: The clip has to sit over the socket's latch; this plug is keyed and won't go in the other way round.
reversed.ramp: The ridge on the plug has to slide along the header's guide; turn it round.
reversed.pin: The blanked hole on the plug has to line up with the header's missing pin; turn it round.

hands.wrongPort: It would fit there, but this lead belongs in another socket. Check the label.
hands.endIn: That end is in. Now the other end.
hands.cpuLeverUp: Lever up. Now open the load plate.
hands.cpuLeverReleased: Lever released. Open the plate to lift the CPU out.
hands.cpuLeverDown: Lever locked. The socket is closed again.
hands.cpuPlateFirst: Close the plate first, then lock the lever under its tab.
hands.cpuPlateNext: The lever is up: open the load plate next.
hands.cpuPlateClosed: Plate down. Now push the lever down and lock it under its tab.
hands.cpuPlateOpenSeated: Plate open. You can lift the CPU straight up and out.
hands.ramPick: Click a memory slot in the view to hold it over that slot. Turn it so the notch faces the slot's key; the clip has to be open.
hands.m2Pick: Click the M.2 slot you want for it. Its notch must match the slot's ridge.
hands.m2NoFit: This drive does not fit {slot}: check its length and type.
hands.m2SlotTaken: {slot} already has a drive. Choose a free slot.
hands.m2HsScrewsFirst: {slot} is under its heatsink. Loosen the heatsink's two screws first.
hands.m2HsLiftNext: Screws loose. Lift the heatsink off.
hands.m2StandFirst: Fit the screw stand at the drive's length hole first.
hands.m2TiltFirst: Tilt the drive up to about 25° before it goes in.
hands.m2Ready: Tilted and over {slot}. Slide it into the slot.
hands.m2PressFlat: It's in {slot} at an angle. Press it flat.
hands.m2LatchNow: Flat. Turn the Q-Latch clockwise to hold it.
hands.m2ScrewNow: Flat on the stand. Screw it down.
hands.m2FilmNext: Held. Peel the plastic film off the heatsink's thermal pad.
hands.m2Done: Heatsink screwed down. The drive is in.
hands.ramClipBlocked: That clip can't move like that now: a module is resting in the slot. Press it in, or lift it out.
hands.ramNoSlot: It isn't over a slot yet. Click a memory slot in the view to hold it there.
hands.ramSlotTaken: {slot} already has a module. Choose a free slot.
hands.ramResting: It rests in {slot}. Now press it straight down until the clip locks.
hands.ramNotRecommended: It fits. For {n} module(s) the manual recommends {rec}; this slot works, but may not give the best (dual-channel) setup.
hands.ramLifted: Out of the slot and in your hand, right above it.

explainText.socket: A CPU fits only the socket it was made for: the pins and the notches differ.
explainText.memory: DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5 have the notch in different places, so a module only fits its own generation.
explainText.size: ATX, micro-ATX and Mini-ITX are sizes, not speed. A case lists the sizes it takes.
explainText.length: The card's length must be at most the case's limit.
explainText.radiator: Each case position lists the radiator sizes it takes (120, 240, 280 …).
explainText.power: The estimate is CPU maximum power + card power + 50 W for the rest. A larger PSU is never a problem.
explainText.storage: M.2 is a shape; NVMe and SATA are interfaces. 2.5 and 3.5 inch drives use SATA cables.
explainText.fans: Each fan needs a position of its size and a header. Extra fans need a hub.
explainText.bios: A new CPU on an older board may need a BIOS update first.
explainText.cooler: A cooler lists the sockets it mounts on, and its height must fit the case.
explainText.general: Check the part's specifications against the other part's limits.

substeps.cpuLever: Lift the socket lever and open the load plate.
substeps.cpuAlign: Match the gold triangle to the socket corner; line up the notches.
substeps.cpuLower: Lower the CPU straight down. Never press or slide it.
substeps.cpuClose: Close the plate and lock the lever (the cover pops off).
substeps.ramNotch: Line up the notch with the key in the slot.
substeps.ramPress: Press both ends down until the latches click.
substeps.m2Latch: Open the M.2 latch or remove its screw.
substeps.m2Angle: Slide the drive into the slot at about 30°.
substeps.m2Secure: Press it flat and close the latch or screw.
substeps.driveTray: Put the drive in a bay or tray of its size.
substeps.driveScrews: Fix it with the tray's pins or screws.
substeps.pasteCheck: Thermal paste: a pea-sized dot on the CPU, unless the cooler's base already has it (the Freezer 7 X does). Never both.
substeps.coolerFilm: Peel the protective film off the cooler's base.
substeps.coolerBracket: Fit the backplate and mounting brackets for this socket.
substeps.coolerDiagonal: Tighten the screws a little at a time, in a diagonal order.
substeps.radiatorMount: Screw the radiator into its case position, hoses down or to the side.
substeps.fanDirection: Fans blow through the radiator in the chosen direction (front = air in).
substeps.standoffs: Check the standoffs match the board's holes (no extra standoffs).
substeps.ioShield: Fit the I/O shield if the board's is not built in.
substeps.boardAlign: Lower the board, ports into the shield, holes over standoffs.
substeps.boardScrews: Screw the board down, not too tight.
substeps.slotCovers: Remove the case's slot covers for the card's width.
substeps.gpuPress: Press the card straight in until the latch clicks.
substeps.gpuBracket: Screw the bracket to the case.
substeps.psuFan: Point the PSU fan at the case's dust filter (usually down).
substeps.psuSlide: Slide the PSU into its bay.
substeps.psuScrews: Fix it with four screws at the back.
substeps.fanArrows: Check the arrows on the frame: front fans blow in, rear and top blow out.
substeps.fanScrews: Screw the fan to its position.
substeps.title: Steps
substeps.tickAll: Tick each step, then fit the part.

hands.title: Hands-on
hands.pressIn: Press it in until it clicks
hands.keys: Keys: Q/E turn · arrows move · Enter lowers
hands.markCpu: Match the CPU's gold corner triangle with the socket's mark. The CPU has flat pads; the pins are in the socket, so never touch or slide over them.
hands.markRam: The notch is off centre: it meets the slot's key only one way round.
hands.takeOther: The other CPU is in the socket. Open the plate and lift it out first.
hands.unverified: The latch arrangement on this board is not shown in its manual; one latch is drawn.
hands.note: Educational simulation: it does not reproduce insertion force.
hands.removeCovers: Unscrew and remove the two slot covers
hands.releasePcie: Press the PCIe latch to release the card
hands.pushCard: Push the card into the slot
hands.screwBracket: Screw the bracket to the case
hands.markGpu: Line up two things before pushing: the gold edge connector with the slot, and the metal bracket with the opening where the covers were.
hands.gpuSource: Slot latch: ASUS TUF GAMING B760-PLUS WIFI manual (E21279), p. 2-19 — push the latch fully, release it to remove the card. The two-cover count and screw positions vary by case and are shown schematically.
hands.closeQLatch: Press the drive flat and turn the Q-Latch to lock
hands.m2Film: Peel the film off the heatsink's thermal pad
hands.m2Stand: Fit the screw stand at the drive's length hole
hands.m2Tilt: Tilt the drive up to about 25°
hands.slideIn: Slide it into the slot at an angle
hands.markM2: The drive's connector has a notch (M key) that matches a ridge in the slot: the label side up, gold contacts towards the slot. It goes in at about 20–30°, then is pressed flat.
hands.m2Source: Q-Latch steps: ASUS TUF GAMING Z790-PLUS WIFI manual (E21279), p. 2-8. The insertion angle is typical, not a figure from the manual.
hands.applyPaste: Put a pea-sized drop of paste on the CPU
hands.peelFilm: Peel the film off the cooler's plate
hands.checkStandoffs: Check the standoffs match the board's holes
hands.fitIoShield: Press the I/O shield into the case
hands.psuFanDown: Turn the PSU: fan facing down
hands.psuFanUp: Turn the PSU: fan facing up
hands.fanIntake: Turn the fan: air into the case
hands.fanExhaust: Turn the fan: air out of the case

place.cooler: Lower the cooler onto the CPU
place.motherboard: Lower the board onto the standoffs
place.psu: Slide the PSU into its bay
place.fan: Hold the fan to its mount
place.liquid: Fit the pump block and the radiator

why.cooler: Paste fills the tiny gaps between the CPU and the cooler. Tighten the screws across the diagonal so the plate meets the CPU evenly. Note: ARCTIC's own LGA1700 instructions for the Freezer 36 and Liquid Freezer III replace the socket's loading mechanism with a contact frame (support.arctic.de); the lab keeps the board's plate and models only the four screws.
why.motherboard: The board sits on standoffs so it never touches the metal tray. Some boards come with the I/O shield already fixed to them (the TUF GAMING Z790-PLUS WIFI does); fitting a separate one then is a mistake.
why.psu: With a filtered vent under the bay, the fan faces down and draws cool air from outside (Corsair's guidance; the 4000D Airflow has that filter). Where the vent is not recorded, either way is accepted.
why.fan: The arrows on the fan's frame show which way air moves. Front and bottom positions pull air in; rear and top blow it out.

hands.prepNote: Each step changes the build and is saved; Undo takes it back. The screw count is the place's own; the force is not simulated.
hands.liquidNote: The pump block and radiator go in as one step here (block screws, radiator screws, and the case fans the radiator displaces are moved for you). Tube routing is not modelled.
hands.captive: This lead is fixed inside the power supply (captive): only its device end plugs in, and it cannot be taken off the PSU.
hands.plugReversed: Plug turned the wrong way: its clip or key is on the far side
hands.plugMatched: Plug turned so its clip or key matches the socket
hands.plugIn: Push it in until it clicks
hands.plugNote: Pick the socket by its label, match the clip to the latch (or the ridge to the guide), then push straight in. Only the planned socket is accepted; push force is not simulated.
hands.coversLater: once the board is in the case
hands.gpuBoardFirst: The card goes in after the board is in the case: its bracket has to meet the case's rear opening.
hands.inScene: Click the lever and the plate in the 3D view, then click the open socket to bring the CPU over it. The action above the view does the same steps, one at a time.
hands.releaseLever: Release the lever and lift it
hands.lockLever: Push the lever down and lock it under its tab
hands.lowerZif: Lower the lever and lock it
hands.lgaSource: Intel socket steps: ASUS TUF GAMING Z790-PLUS WIFI manual E21279 pp. 2-1–2-2 and ASUS FAQ 1047659: hold the lever as you release it, lift it, then the plate; to close, plate first, then lock the lever under its tab — the protective cover then pops off (keep it). The same mechanism is used for the LGA1150 board (ASUS H81M-K). The TUF lever protector is not modelled.
hands.zifSource: AM4: ASUS FAQ 1047659 — lift the lever to 90°, match the CPU triangle to the socket's corner, lower the CPU straight down, lower the lever.
hands.ramOffRecommendation: With this slot the layout isn't the recommended one; it still works.
hands.ramInScene: Click a slot in the 3D view to hold the module over it, then click its clips or the slot again for each next step. The buttons above the view and the keys do the same checked steps.
hands.slotTakenHint: {slot} already has a module. Move to a free slot.
hands.notchReversed: Turned the wrong way: the notch is at the other end
hands.slotPrev: Move across, towards the previous slot
hands.slotNext: Move across, towards the next slot
hands.ramKeys: Keys in the view: ←/→ across the slots, ↑/↓ along, Q or E turns it round, Enter lowers.
hands.ramPartial: It rests in the slot but is not in yet: press it straight down until the clip locks.
hands.ramSeatedHint: Home and locked. To take it out: open the clip, then lift it straight up.

learning.name: Virtual Training Environment (VTE)
learning.tagline: Build your PC. Write your code. Find your way.
learning.intro: A place to try, learn, and make things work—with a little helper when you need one.
learning.helpStartDetail: A clear first step, a small example, then your turn.
learning.selfStartDetail: Choose a lab and try your ideas at your own pace.
learning.chooseTitle: What would you like to try?
learning.startSteps: 1. Choose code or PC assembly. 2. Try a small step. 3. Run it, then ask the helper if you get stuck.
learning.helperNote: The little robot in the corner is here whenever you need help.
learning.codeTitle: A little code. A real result.
learning.codeIntro: Pick a language, write something, and run it. Learn with examples or build your own idea.

tasks.0: Run a greeting, then change the message to your own name.
tasks.1: Use a function to calculate a result. Change the numbers and predict the answer.
tasks.2: Work with a list. Add a value and decide which results should appear.
tasks.3: Model a real task with structured code. Add one behavior and explain how it works.

webTasks.0: Make a heading and a paragraph. Change the words and the heading color.
webTasks.1: Create a card with HTML and CSS. Add another detail and adjust the spacing.
webTasks.2: Make a responsive grid. Add a card and compare different widths.
webTasks.3: Build a form with clear labels and keyboard focus. Try submitting it with an empty field.

learning.freeNote: This space is yours. Try a calculator, a small page, or any idea you like. Language changes keep a separate draft.
learning.runtimeLoading: Preparing the language for the first run…
learning.runError: The program stopped. Read the error or ask the helper.
learning.runnerUnavailable: This language’s runner is unavailable. Your code has been kept.
learning.serverTrackUnavailable: Running {language} needs a code runner that this site doesn’t have. You can still read and edit the code here. To run code, choose JavaScript, TypeScript or Python.
learning.stopped: Stopped. You can edit and run again.
learning.outputEmpty: Your program’s output will appear here.
learning.aiNotConfigured: Real AI review needs a provider connection. Built-in error guidance is available now.
learning.aiUnavailable: AI review is unavailable right now. Here is the built-in guidance.
learning.typoHelp: There may be a small spelling mistake in a command. Check {token}. You can review the suggested change and apply it, then run again.
learning.errorHelp: The checker reported an issue near line {line}: {message}. Check that line and the one before it, then run again.
learning.generalHelp: Try running the code first. Read the first error, check names and punctuation, and change one thing at a time. If it runs, change a value and predict the new result.
learning.privacy: Code runs in an isolated learning environment. Only asking the helper sends the current file and error to a configured AI provider. AI suggestions are untested until you run them.
learning.footer: Try it. Understand it. Make it work.
learning.previewReady: Your page is live. Edit the code and run again to refresh it.
learning.pcCardText: Choose what the computer is for, pick compatible parts, then assemble them hands-on: open the socket, line up the CPU's triangle, press memory home, connect the leads and start it.
